prompt:
Challenge C088-CH2: Membranes in dairy plants foul quickly and need cleaning every week.
Detail: At two dairy plants we service — one near Temerin, one outside

content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Membrane fouling was characterised by trans-membrane pressure increase during continuous operation with enzyme-laden suspensions, and a daily backwash protocol maintained acceptable flux over the operating period.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-03519","field":"abstract","quote":"Membrane fouling was characterised by trans-membrane pressure increase; a daily 15 min backwash protocol maintained acceptable flux"}]},{"text":"Cleaning protocols for ultrafiltration membranes fouled with dairy process streams were evaluated, showing that sodium hydroxide and hypochlorite treatments achieved high flux recovery but affected membrane lifetime.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-03378","field":"abstract","quote":"Three laboratory-scale cleaning protocols were evaluated for polyethersulphone and ceramic ultrafiltration membranes fouled with skim milk"}]},{"text":"Enzyme adsorption kinetics and substrate structural characterisation after mild pre-treatment are investigated to understand how inhibition and substrate accessibility affect enzymatic processes.","sources":[{"id":"R0281","field":"bio","quote":"His group investigates enzymatic saccharification of lignocellulosic biomass, focusing on inhibition modelling, substrate structural characterisation"}]}],"fit":"partial","fitReason":"The researcher has direct experience with membrane fouling characterisation and CIP protocols in dairy applications [SYN-PUB-03378] and enzyme adsorption mechanisms [R0281], but the publications focus on enzymatic biorefinery processes and cleaning optimisation rather than the biological mechanisms of protein-fat-sugar gel layer formation in dairy MBRs."}
